Idle Wizard, developed and published by TwoWizards, is one of those rare incremental games that quietly establishes itself as a genre staple through sheer depth and longevity. At first glance, it appears to follow the familiar formula of watching resources accumulate and periodically resetting for larger rewards. However, beneath its modest presentation lies an intricate web of mechanics that continually expands over dozens, if not hundreds, of hours. Rather than relying on flashy visuals or constant action, the game embraces the fantasy of mastering the arcane arts through careful planning, experimentation, and endless progression.

Players begin their journey as a novice magician and gradually unlock an extensive roster of magical classes, each fundamentally changing how the game is approached. Whether focusing on rapid advancement, sustained growth, or specialized resource generation,

reviews.title: Try this game please!
reviews.text:
This game is like a breathe of fresh air for idle/tapper games. It reminds me why I fell in love with the genre in the first place. I haven’t felt the overwhelming need to pay for anything in this game to progress, in facts the game has a system for active or passives users to enjoy and it helpfully describes that in the games description. If you’ve been looking for a new game to pass the time then please try this one. We need more games like this. 
A note to the developer: if the spell section is listed in a specific way then I understand, I just didn’t know I could scroll down and purchase other spells sooner to help me progress faster. It may be helpful to others if you could put spells in a purchase order from least expensive to most. If the list is specifically placed due to other reasons then I understand and hopefully this review helps those that didn’t know this yet!
Thank you fo

reviews.title: Finally, an idle game not fueled by a developer's greed
reviews.text:
When I mention idle games to my friends, they think I'm insane because they're known as a cesspool of timewalls, paywalls, and intense greed from developers in the form of $9.99 for this, $4.99 for that, five minutes of ads for that other thing. All I really want from idle games is a relaxing and chill experience, and I'm even sick of those cash-grabs. 

And then you have this game: Idle Wizard, a Fair Play Game. It captures all the thrills of similar games (and even uses the formula that put Egg, Inc. on the map), and takes out the $9.99. Even ads are an optional feature of the game, though highly rewarding for those who choose to build around ads, yet the game is still competent and fun to play. 

Then you have the customization in the form of items and ancient mana (think Epic Upgrades and Golden Eggs), in that every aspect of the game can be upgraded permanently beyond prestiges, fro

reviews.title: Fun game, fun progression
reviews.text:
I think overall the game is fun and has a good aesthetic. I’d recommend anyone that likes incremental games to definitely try it. 

I’d like to see an option to “buy” it and remove ads, as they’re always intrusive. I know it is the “mobile way” but that doesn’t make ads any less obtrusive when asked “waste X time watching this ad, get rewarded with Y stuff”.  It’s still ultimately a waste of time even if it gives players in-game items. I guess it’s up to the dev to decide what works best for them vs what people will put up with to play their game. I’m currently still playing it but after a while the ads are annoying and I can see myself stopping relatively soon because of it. On the flip side, I’m sure it is hard as a dev to find the financial model that works for their app. 

Anyway. Overall, I’d recommend anyone try the game as the game itself seems pretty fun.

reviews.title: Great idle game but I need more!!!
reviews.text: Lots to upgrade and items can be leveled strategically. No pay to win aspects, easy on the ads with no required viewing. The only thing missing is more content as after a few hours it can get a little repetitive. Maybe give the option to hire apprentices that auto click for you or auto level up the cheapest skill or raise the rates for flying orbs, maybe make them stay after regression but they only stick to a specific orb type. Maybe a side mode you can tame monsters to follow you who you can send off on missions for more item upgrade materials or other stuff. Lots of potential. Would like to see this game grow.

reviews.title: Great Idle Game
reviews.text:
First of all, the fact that you don’t HAVE to watch ads, but worth the few seconds to do so is awesome. I don’t generally give reviews, and mostly because the game can be amazing but it’s got a paywall or constant ads and I delete the thing and move on. This one, I’ve been messing with all day. Only missing a help menu, as I’m still confused about a few things but I’ll figure it out. Anyone that likes idle games for picking up on break or lunch or just when having idle time, this is definitely worth checking out.

Many other games could learn from the way the developers put the ads out there on this game. Kudos to the development team here.

reviews.title: Phenomenal Game, Ads are not annoying
reviews.text: Ok so I downloaded this game thinking it’d be a quirky wizard incremental, but I was quickly surprised with the depth, quality, and immersion. There is careful thought in the design of the gameplay here. The biggest point for me here is that the ads aren’t randomly shoved down your throat, they’re all optional (portal pops up, your choice to tap it, and you choose the rewards you want from the ad)! There are also bonus rewards/milestones for how many ads you decide to watch. I think the best part though is that the ads are tied into the lore, they don’t break the immersion. When a game is handled this way, it is so refreshing!

reviews.title: This game has been on my phone longer than any other.
reviews.text:
I’ve played Idle Magic Clicker / wizard for literal years now, and it is the only game that I’ll always come back to. 
There is not much I can do anymore with gameplay but that doesn’t matter to me. I play this when I’m upset to calm down, I play it when I need to wait just a few more minutes for something in real life.
It inspires me to do art and to create because seemingly one person made this thing and it matters so much to me.
Rene, I hope you’re proud of this game. I hope you come back to the reviews sometime and see that it’s loved.  Thank you.

2. I love the story behind the game, little details like that make games so much more enjoyable and reading the orbs each level up is fun! Keep the story going!!

3. Maybe develop a weekly event world, I don’t know if that would or would not be liked by the popular vote, so maybe only test this and see how it w

reviews.title: So good!
reviews.text:
I have really grown to love this game! So satisfying to keep clicking :) 
One note to the developer: I would not mind paying for the game to be able to skip ads that offer boosts. 
Like a “no ads” cost, that makes us be able to still get the boosts but not have to watch the ads.
The reason I’m asking for this option is because my autistic 7 year old loves to click around in this game, and the ads are long and I have to click through them so my son can continue playing.

reviews.title: This is what an idle game should be
reviews.text:
No forced ads! That’s the first and most important thing I will say. 
Most developers today seem to not be aware how much people hate forced ads. Or worse, they don’t care. My favorite genre of mobile games is idle/incremental/clicker, but the first time a game forces me to watch an ad, I delete it. Games like this one, that don’t force me to watch ads, I’ll watch lots of ads because it’s my choice. 
This developer got it right, and I’m sure they will earn plenty from me.

reviews.title: PLEASE READ REVIEWERS/PLAYERS
reviews.text:
First off, I want to commend the complete lack of cash grabs and paywalls and monetary purchases. Beautiful. Truly.

To the players on iPhone like myself waiting for the devs to add notch support, if you slide up from the bottom, as though to enter app select, or whatever it’s called, where you can close apps, or switch back and forth. Just slide up a little bit, and it gives you a look at your blue orb count. A little annoying, but gives you that little bit of info.

Fun idle game! The progression is familiar (think Egg Inc) but unique, and the business model is very user friendly, with the only ads being optional for rewards. I suggest a few important features be added through updates:

-Notch support - please slide down the upper menu a little bit! Orb charges are completely covered by the notch on my iPhone X
-A menu for viewing stats - power generation, generation speed, max overcharge, overcharge per shot, etc. I like stat menus in idle games because they help me target weak spots in production, and just generally know what is going on. 
-An option to “buy” the game to make all optional ad rewards be claimable without watching an ad. Whatever you think is reasonable, probably based on your average ad income per user. I’m always happy to pay in the realm of $5 for this, maybe more. 

Thank you!

reviews.title: Finally
reviews.text: I won’t lie, when I saw this game, I had expected there to be a bunch of ads. So when I read some other reviews saying there weren’t any, I was pretty excited. All ads are clearly identifiable. Also, you get rewarded, not just with a small amount of in game currency, but when you watch a specific amount of ads (5) you get another reward! This game is a lot of fun and I’m personally addicted.

reviews.title: Must Play for Fans of Idle Games
reviews.text:
If you like idle games and are sick of ads, you’ve got to give this one a go.  It’s so refreshing to be able to choose if you want to watch ads for specific rewards or just skip them.  And they aren’t game changers, neither is the game pay2win. 

The gameplay is appealing, the visuals and sound quality are great, and the pacing is excellent.

reviews.title: Focus Breaks
reviews.text: I’ve reset several times with more focus stones but the game caps out at a certain point because I cannot break through after a certain point. I have currently 210,000 % increase from focus but it doesn’t change how far I can get. I barely make 10AD. Then I buy power focus increase of 1% per stone and it doesn’t change production. Something about the math is broken which is frustrating. The game is fun for about a day before you get trapped in an endless cycle.

reviews.title: Good way to pass the time
reviews.text: This game is as good or better than many others which constantly tempt you with some sort of pay-to-win mechanic, and all advertisements are optional. There is a minor issue with the top resource bar being partly obscured by the notch on newer iPhones, but it isn’t game breaking. A slight repositioning of said resource bar would be appreciated, and likely change my rating from four to five stars.

reviews.title: Ads are actually optional

It does have ads to get boosts but one, what you get is definitely worth the 30 seconds, and two, you can choose to just not watch the ad and it doesn’t throw you into a secondary ad to cover you not watching the original.

reviews.title: Absolutely what it says on the tin
reviews.text:
Very straightforward idle with good upgrades setup and even a little thought to tailor your playstyle. I've only played a few days and I'm not sure what (if any) mechanics exist past the overall basic "make number bigger", "buy next upgrade", and "sphere teleport/focus".. not that it's not a grind but I believe the game may reach an end fairly quickly once I get to numbers for the biggest visible upgrades. I could be completely wrong and in store for a surprise.
 Amusingly while it's advertised as nothing to pay for, this is one I would absolutely throw $5-$8 at to support, maybe for "don't have to watch ads for bonus/rift/offline" (not sure how much an ad makes them? probably equivalent to about 250-400 watches; saving me 150-250 mins of ad watching.. vs 12/day boost+20~rifts/etc). Watching ads isn't necessary but you're not going to avoid them if you want items in any quick timeframe.
